youtube.title: The World's Most Famous Bandleader Flew Into the Clouds and Vanished | Glenn Miller
youtube.description:
On 15 December 1944, Major Glenn Miller, leader of the US Army Air Force band, left RAF Twinwood Farm in Bedfordshire aboard a single-engine UC-64 Norseman bound for Paris, with Lt. Col. Norman Baessell and pilot Flight Officer John Morgan. The weather was poor after days of fog. The aircraft was seen heading out over the Channel but never reached Paris, and no wreckage or bodies were ever found. With the Battle of the Bulge under way, his disappearance was not reported for days. Decades later, RAF navigator Fred Shaw claimed bombs jettisoned by Lancasters returning from an aborted raid hit a small plane over the Channel, but no record of that account exists from before the 1950s. Others blame the weather or a mechanical fault.

📂 Case File #029: The Glenn Miller Mystery

Sources: Skeptoid #406, "The Disappearance of Glenn Miller"; Tara Ross, "This Day in History: Glenn Miller disappears"; This Day in Aviation, 15 December 1944.
